title: Generate Parentheses
statement:
Given `n` pairs of parentheses, build every string of length `2n` that is well formed: reading left to right, the number of `(` characters seen so far is never smaller than the number of `)` characters seen so far, and the two counts are equal at the end.

Return all such strings in ascending lexicographic order, where `(` sorts before `)`.

Constraints: `1 <= n <= 8`.

constraints: Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: A prefix is worth extending only while it can still be completed; think about which prefixes can never be fixed by adding more characters.
Track how many '(' and ')' you have placed so far: you may open while open < n and you may close while close < open.
Every leaf of that search tree is one answer of length 2n, and the leaves arrive in lexicographic order when '(' is tried before ')'.

editorial.approach: The brute force enumerates all 2^(2n) strings of length 2n over the two bracket characters, validates each with a single balance counter that must never go negative and must finish at zero, and keeps the survivors, sorting at the end. Nothing is pruned. The optimal version grows candidates one character at a time and only extends a prefix that can still be completed: another pair may be opened while open < n, and a bracket may be closed while close < open, so every node of the search tree is already a valid prefix and each leaf is one finished answer. The leaf count is the n-th Catalan number C(n) = (2n choose n) / (n + 1) instead of 2^(2n); at n = 8 that is 1430 validated leaves against 65536 raw candidates.
editorial.why_optimal: The output itself has C(n) strings of length 2n, so any correct solution rebuilds C(n) * n characters and cannot beat O(C(n) * n) time; the backtracking tree is exactly the set of valid prefixes, so it touches no invalid branch and matches that bound. Space is the answer list plus a depth-2n buffer. The exponential version is only tolerable because 2^16 is small; the same loop at n = 20 would iterate a million million candidates.
editorial.pitfalls: Dropping the close < open guard produces branches such as ')' first, wasting the whole subtree on strings that can only fail later. Testing balance == 0 or open == n for termination instead of length == 2n can end the recursion on a short prefix. Forgetting cur.pop() after a recursive call leaks characters into sibling branches and inflates every later answer. And because both implementations must return the same list, the promised order has to be enforced identically: generation that tries '(' before ')' already emits lexicographic order, but sorting in both implementations removes any dependency on that property.

solutions.title: Brute Force
solutions.complexity: Time: O(4^n * n) | Space: O(C(n) * n)

solutions.title: Optimal
solutions.complexity: Time: O(C(n) * n) | Space: O(C(n) * n)
